text:
Alicia: FYI discovered a parity issue between node SDK and REST: sdk.deleteRoute('staging-xyz') returns success even when route doesn't exist. sample-app onboarding silently skips recreation.

Jamie: oh no. which SDK version and env?

Alicia: sdk@2.4.0, node 18, staging. Minimal repro: 
```js
await client.routes.delete({ routeId: 'not-real' }) // -> { success: true }
```
versus curl -> 404.

Tariq: platform sometimes returns 204 on deletes for absent resources, but 404 is expected in this case. Could the SDK be normalizing 404 -> 200 for idempotency?

Alicia: logs show client layer reporting a handled 204 though curl shows 404. so mapping happening client-side.

Maya: workaround: sample-app will now verify existence after delete and recreate if missing. pushing fix to branch onboarding/ensure-route.

Jamie: I opened RED-4571 and a draft PR to change SDK behavior: stop auto-converting non-2xx to success for delete endpoints. adding rawStatus to responses and throwing on 404 by default. PR: https://github.com/redwood/inference-sdk/pull/1002

deploy-bot: Deployed sample-app patch to staging (canary 1/5).

Tariq: we should add unit tests that simulate 404 from server and assert SDK throws. Also add an integration test for sample-app onboarding to catch this.

Alicia: agreed. also add migration note in changelog: some callers expect idempotent behavior and will need to opt-in.

Jamie: plan: patch release 2.4.1, update sample-app onboarding fallback in a hotfix. ETA tomorrow morning.

Maya: will monitor staging and rollback if churn. :eyes:

Alicia: thanks team :thumbsup:
